human_tolerance.notes: Roosts in tree hollows and buildings, and forages at night. The block behavior treats daylight as roost time.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: October-November births are reported for the species. Winter hibernation is documented for cooler southern Australian populations, but this record-wide phase cannot encode that regional distinction.

vocalizations.description: Ultrasonic echolocation pulses used to locate prey and avoid obstacles.

taxonomy.note: GBIF API response checked 2026-10-31: accepted Chalinolobus morio at species rank; canonical name and family/order/class match the record.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2432295 resolves to accepted species Chalinolobus morio. iNaturalist taxon 40543 is active and also resolves to this species.

range.note: The State of Victoria factsheet describes the species as widespread across eastern and southern Australia and records it in the Northern Territory; the licensed Wikipedia article says it is found only in Australia. The country-level native range is AU. Its elevation record is described as reaching at least 1,570 m, so no upper elevation bound is stored.

traits.limb_count.note: Bat has two forelimbs modified as wings and two hindlimbs; schema limb count counts all four limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Powered flight is described directly. Walking is an authored secondary mode for short ground movement; the selected program uses flight for travel and feeding.

traits.nest_type.note: Uses tree hollows and buildings as day roosts; mapped to the closest supported cavity option.

traits.size_class.note: Classified Tiny from the reported 8 g adult mass.

traits.mass_kg.note: Converted the paper's species-level 8 g mass to 0.008 kg.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Converted the factsheet's non-pregnant adult range of 8-11 g to kg.

traits.length_m.note: Converted the factsheet's 60 mm body length to 0.06 m; that source does not specify whether this is a mean or a maximum.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Uses the paper's 2.0-year mean life expectancy after banding for resident C. morio at one northeastern NSW forest site. This is an empirical typical-wild-lifespan proxy, not a maximum; apparent-survival estimates can underestimate true life expectancy and the study is site-specific.

traits.diet.note: The factsheet says insects; the Wikipedia article says prey consists almost entirely of moths. The schema has no moth category, so the insectivorous diet is represented as 100% invertebrate.

traits.social.note: The factsheet reports daytime roost colonies of about 10 to 20; the schema range represents that typical roost group, not exceptional larger caves or solitary males.

traits.activity_pattern.note: The factsheet says the bats roost and sleep during the day and emerge at night to feed.

traits.defense.note: Flee response is an authored simulation judgment; the species sources do not describe a defense response.

traits.wariness.note: Authored simulation judgment; no source provides a wariness measure.

habitat.use.note: Aerial 0.8 and arboreal 0.2 are authored habitat-use shares, based on aerial foraging and tree/building roosting. No source measures proportional time by stratum.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Tree hollows and buildings map to cavity shelter.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Use of buildings and records from Melbourne suburbs support the Adapter classification; light_max is an authored conservative simulation setting.

seasonal.strategy.note: Set ActiveYearRound for the country-level record because winter hibernation is only documented for cooler southern Australian populations and the schema cannot apply that population-specific strategy to part of the national range. The activity curve remains observation-derived and shows reduced winter detections; this record does not simulate the southern hibernation period.

seasonal.phases.note: October-November birth timing converted to a broad AU breeding interval; the factsheet also reports winter hibernation in cooler southern populations, which is a known but unrepresented regional difference.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Adult only; juvenile duration is not supplied by the cited open sources.

activity.AU.note: Fetched from observation histograms; counts and usability flags are retained in the query metadata. Observation frequency is an imperfect proxy for activity.

behavior.note: Species-local program flies and feeds after dusk, roosts at daylight, and flees by flight. It represents night/day timing and aerial insect feeding; it does not model winter hibernation.

vocalizations.note: The factsheet describes echolocation pulses at approximately 50 kHz; represented as an ultrasonic call with no emitted audible frequency data.

look.note: Brown fur, domed head, and small facial lobes are source-described. Stylized proportions, part placement, and sRGB values are authored visual judgments.
